title: Rabbi Yose ben HaChotef Efrati
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben HaChotef Efrati, a Tanna mentioned in the Mishnah. In Kilayim 3:7 he transmits in Rabbi Yishmael’s name and disagrees with Rabbi Meir: Rabbi Meir says in Rabbi Yishmael’s name, three gourds to every beit seah, while Rabbi Yose ben HaChotef says in Rabbi Yishmael’s name, three gourds to every beit kor.

At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 3, Rabbi Yose son of Bun says: “See the difference between Rabbi Yishmael’s earlier and later teaching: at first a beit kor, afterward a beit seah.” Hyman infers that Rabbi Yose ben HaChotef studied with Rabbi Yishmael first, and Rabbi Meir did so afterward. Rabbi Shimshon copies the Jerusalem Talmud in reverse, with Rabbi Meir studying first.

notes.text: The chronological inference is that Yose studied with Yishmael first and Meir afterward; it does not make Meir Yose’s teacher. The reverse order is attributed to Rabbi Shimshon’s Mishnah commentary. The heading’s provisional origin remains preserved.

Mishnah Kilayim 3:7 directly names Yose ben HaChotef Efrati and contrasts three gourds per beit seah with three per beit kor. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud chapter 3 ending gives Yose son of Bun’s earlier/later comparison. Hyman’s inference about the order in which Yose and Meir studied with Yishmael remains his. The exact Rabbi Shimshon commentary was not inspected; the heading’s historical provisional status remains preserved.
